Provenance as product. Every line points home.

The Flow

A shipment becomes a fact. A fact meets the rules.
The rules produce a packet.

  1. I

    Documents

    Invoices, bills of lading, packing lists, certificates of origin. In any format your team already uses.

  2. II

    Reading

    Drona parses each document into a structured shipment fact model — bounded, source-located, replayable.

  3. III

    States

    Every obligation resolves to Open, Blocked, Conditional, or Unclear against the live rule pack for your jurisdiction.

  4. IV

    Review

    A human reviewer attests. The system records who, when, and on what evidence.

  5. V

    Packet

    Out: a hash-chained, source-stamped packet you can hand to a customs officer, an underwriter, or a banker — and defend three years from now.

Your junior analyst. On shift forever.

The Lanes

We start narrow. Deliberately.

TradeWatch ships first to the trade lanes where the cost of being wrong is highest and the evidence trail is longest.

01

EV Exporters

Electric vehicles moving between India, the EU, and the US — inbound or outbound — where battery provenance, lithium chain-of-custody, and dual-use controls collide.

02

Complex Issues

Where legal, regulatory, and customs questions tangle, our depth makes the hard call defensible — like a contestable HS classification that would otherwise become a Section 149 amendment six months later.

03

L/C Pre-Presentation

Before your banker presents, every document is checked against the credit against the rule pack. Six weeks from kickoff to first live packet.

04

Marine Cargo

Underwriting-grade evidence: compliance status, loss history, customs clearance probability — packaged for the broker.

05

Shipping Bill Readiness

Pre-filing reconciliation between what you're declaring, what you're shipping, and what India permits.

06

e-BRC / RoDTEP Closing

Closing-loop evidence so your incentives don't get clawed back at audit.

Sreenath Govindarajan

Founder, Kanan Labs

Cross-border law · AI governance · Regulatory strategy · Trade intelligence

The Operating Doctrine

I founded Kanan Labs from a simple conviction: cross-border trade is no longer governed only by access, price, and logistics. It is increasingly governed by whether a firm can prove its position across regulators, brokers, banks, insurers, and supply-chain counterparties.

My training across multiple legal systems shaped how I understand this problem. Rules do not operate in isolation. They move through institutions, documents, incentives, and evidentiary burdens. Kanan is being built to turn that complexity into structured intelligence that firms can actually use.

  1. I

    Evidence before automation

    We do not treat trade documentation as form generation. We treat it as an evidence system.

  2. II

    Reasoning before output

    Every packet should preserve the source, the rule, the reasoning path, and the reviewer decision.

  3. III

    Infrastructure before interface

    TradeWatch is the first deployment. The larger undertaking is an intelligence layer for regulated trade.
